claims.text: InMemoryEventStore.Load replays the order's whole stream (FromEvents(ReadStream(orderId))) on every call.

OrderSnapshots.Save calls store.Save(order) first, then takes order.ToSnapshot() when order.Version minus the latest snapshot's Version (0 if none) is >= every; it keeps only the latest snapshot per order in an in-memory Dictionary.
OrderSnapshot is a record of OrderId, CustomerId, TotalVnd, Status, Version; EventSourcedOrder.ToSnapshot copies Id, CustomerId, TotalVnd, Status, Version into it.

OrderSnapshots.Load: with no snapshot, reads the whole stream and calls FromEvents; with one, calls ReadStream(orderId, afterVersion: snapshot.Version) and FromSnapshot; both set EventsReplayedByLastLoad to the number of events read.
InMemoryEventStore.ReadStream(orderId, afterVersion) returns the stream skipping its first afterVersion events.

FromSnapshot sets Id, CustomerId, TotalVnd, Status and Version from the snapshot, then applies each later event with the private Apply used by FromEvents; since Version is restored, LoadedVersion (Version - NewEvents.Count) gives Append the right expected version.

Append throws StreamConcurrencyException when the stream's event count differs from the order's loaded version (another save appended since the load); OrderSnapshots.Save then exits before the snapshot check, so no snapshot is taken.
DeleteAll clears every snapshot; the next Load of an order replays its whole stream.

Snapshot_LoadsTheSameOrder_AndCanBeDeleted: every 2; order 7 placed, paid, shipped, saved after each; snapshot taken at version 2 after Pay, none after Ship; first Load replays 1 event, after DeleteAll 3; ToSnapshot of both loads are equal.
C# records have value equality: two record instances of the same type with equal property values are equal, so Assert.Equal on two OrderSnapshot records compares their fields.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: Records — Value equality

claims.text: A sample order's stream holds at most three events: Pay only from new, Ship only from paid, Cancel refused when cancelled or shipped.
OrderProjection.Rebuild sets Position to 0 and catches up from the first event of ReadAll; projections track Position over all events, OrderSnapshot stores Version within one stream.

The block '== a snapshot every 2 events' of scripts/design/event-sourcing.sh prints 'with the snapshot: shipped, 1 event replayed' and 'snapshots deleted: shipped, 3 events replayed' for order 7 placed, paid and shipped.

An event store only appends, so deleting events means changing it. A snapshot is a cache of replay: deleting snapshots only slows loads, and after a shape change they are retaken; events keep their stored shape, so new code must still apply it.
Snapshots pay off when an aggregate's stream grows long; for short streams, such as a sample order's, they are extra code to keep correct.
